# About the Author {.unnumbered}

![Photo of Michael Borck](images/author-photo.jpg){fig-alt="Photo of Michael Borck, the author" width=200px fig-align="center"}

**Michael Borck** is a software developer and educator working at the intersection of human expertise and artificial intelligence. He teaches applied AI and AI in business at Curtin University, and runs *The Human Edge* masterclasses through Curtin Executive Education.

*Speak Software: Programming at the Natural-Language Layer* is for readers who will never write code by hand. It treats programming as a management job: you describe what you want, an AI agent builds it, and your work is specification, verification, decomposition, and taste. The hands-on companion is the Speak Software programming labs, a free set of client-brief exercises at [michael-borck.github.io/programming-labs](https://michael-borck.github.io/programming-labs/). The labs supply the doing; this book supplies the why, the guardrails, and the harness the labs leave out, including the slop gate, the evidence-trio linter, and the environment pre-flight in this book's `tools/` folder.

His earlier book, *Conversation, Not Delegation*, argues for treating AI as a thinking partner you converse with. The Python track in this series teaches the language itself for readers who want it under their fingers. *Speak Software* takes the other interface: no syntax, and a department of one to run instead.

Michael builds educational software and resources, and writes about the 80/20 principle in learning and professional judgement.
